name: Barcodes Talk
summary: Authentic UPC and EAN barcodes for retail and Amazon listings. Buy GS1-sourced barcodes for your products as a one-time purchase, without an annual GS1 membership.
best_for: sellers and small brands listing on marketplaces or in independent retail who want authentic, one-time-cost UPC/EAN barcodes without an annual GS1 membership
skip_if: your target retailer or brand registry explicitly requires a GS1-issued company prefix in your own name, then buy direct from GS1
honest_knock: The honest caveat is about fit, not the codes. Some large retailers and brand registries (notably certain Amazon Brand Registry and big-box requirements) increasingly ask for a GS1-issued prefix tied to your own company, and a third-party barcode (legitimate and globally unique as it is) may not satisfy that specific gatekeeping. For most marketplaces and independent retail it's completely fine and far cheaper; just confirm your channel's exact requirement first.

pricing.notes: (prices re-verified 2026-11-26 on barcodestalk.com/buy-barcodes) One-off purchase, no subscription and no renewal. The full published ladder runs eighteen rungs: 1 barcode $5.00; 5 for $10.00 ($2.00 each); 10 for $15.00 ($1.50); 25 for $25.00 ($1.00); 50 for $35.00 ($0.70); 100 for $45.00 ($0.45); 200 for $80.00 ($0.40); 500 for $125.00 ($0.25); 1,000 for $180.00 ($0.18); 1,500 for $225.00 ($0.15); 2,000 for $260.00 ($0.13); 2,500 for $300.00 ($0.12); 5,000 for $500.00 ($0.10); 10,000 for $650.00 ($0.065); 25,000 for $1,200.00 ($0.048); 50,000 for $2,300.00 ($0.046); 75,000 for $3,225.00 ($0.043); and 100,000 for $3,500.00 ($0.035). Larger quantities are quote-only. The unit price drops fastest between one and a hundred codes. Every purchase includes both UPC and EAN formats, high-resolution PNG and EPS images, a Certificate of GTIN Assignment, Excel and PDF spreadsheets of the assigned numbers, instant download, and the vendor's Works for Amazon Guarantee. Prices unchanged since our 5 September reading; the listed image formats changed from EPS and JPEG to PNG and EPS.

compare_with.name: GS1 directly
compare_with.why: GS1 costs more and can carry ongoing fees, but it's the only route when a channel demands a prefix registered to your company

exit_test.what: No account was needed; the tool ran without signing in. On 18 November 2026 the session tested two free tools of Barcodes Talk without an account. The Barcode Quantity Calculator counted 6 codes for a product with 3 sizes and 2 colours in about a minute and recommended the package of 10 Barcodes, which costs $15.00 on the price list, though no price was shown next to the advice. The FNSKU label generator made an on-screen Amazon label for a made up code on an Avery 5160 sheet layout; it was not printed or scanned. The price list matches the dossier, but the page now says PNG & EPS images and gives a different GS1 US starting price than the dossier. Nothing was bought. Account and start: NO account was made and none was used; the free tools of Barcodes Talk run without signing in. Our AI assistant ran the test in our own tab of our browser, starting at 13:20. No cookie banner got in the way (there was a Your Privacy Choices link, not clicked). No e-mail address, phone number, password or card was typed in. The dossier name is Barcodes Talk and the review is on OSM (barcodes-talk-review). Core action 1, Barcode Quantity Calculator (barcodestalk.com/barcode-quantity-calculator), about 13:20 to 13:21, 1 minute, 4 steps: product Blue Snowboard, variation Size = 3 and Color = 2 (through + Add another variation type), Add Product. Result: Total Barcodes Needed 6 UPC/EAN codes, Breakdown Blue Snowboard 6, which is the right count (3 sizes times 2 colours). The tool recommended a package of 10 Barcodes, marked Best Match, with no price next to it, only a green Buy Barcodes button that was not clicked. On the price list 10 Barcodes cost $15.00. The page also shows the example T-Shirt (3 sizes, 4 colors), 12 barcodes needed. Core action 2, Amazon FNSKU label generator (barcodestalk.com/amazon-fnsku-barcode-label-generator), 13:21, 4 steps: the made up FNSKU code X00TEST001, product name Blue Snowboard, condition New, quantity 30 (the default) and the label format Avery 5160, 1" x 2.625" (30 labels/sheet), Amazon Recommended. Generate Label said Label generated successfully! and the preview showed a barcode with X00TEST001, Blue Snowboard and New. Nothing was saved or printed (Save Label, Save JPG and Print / PDF were not used), so the label was only seen on screen and was not scanned. Plans: The Buy Barcodes page (barcodestalk.com/buy-barcodes) was read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 and read again just before this delivery the same day, with the same prices: 1 Barcode $5.00, 5 Barcodes $10.00 ($2.00 ea), 10 Barcodes $15.00 ($1.50 ea), 25 Barcodes $25.00, 50 Barcodes $35.00, 100 Barcodes $45.00, 200 Barcodes $80.00, 500 Barcodes $125.00, 1,000 Barcodes $180.00, 1,500 $225.00, 2,000 $260.00, 2,500 $300.00, 5,000 $500.00, 10,000 $650.00, 25,000 $1,200.00, 50,000 $2,300.00, 75,000 $3,225.00 and 100,000 $3,500.00 ($0.035 ea). Included: UPC & EAN barcodes, PNG & EPS images, a Certificate of GTIN Assignment, Excel & PDF spreadsheets, Works for Amazon Guaranteed and No Renewal Fees or Hidden Charges. The prices match the dossier. No Buy Now button was clicked. Differences on the page against the dossier: the page lists PNG & EPS Images Included, while the dossier says EPS and JPEG. The comparison table on the page gives GS1 US Direct a starting price of US$30 for one GTIN and annual renewal fees of $0 for individual GTINs, with annual fees for Company Prefixes, while the dossier says $250 for 10 plus $50 a year. The site of GS1 US itself was not checked, so which figure is current is not known here. The page also says Accepted by 99% of retailers and asks you to check whether your retailer accepts reseller barcodes. Cancelling: there is no account and no subscription, so there was nothing to cancel. Not tested: a purchase and the checkout, the certificate, the GEPIR registration, the sample package (which may ask for an e-mail address), whether Amazon or Brand Registry accept the codes, a printed or scanned label, and the other free tools (bulk, SKU, QR, country of origin). Clean up: there is no account and no test data was saved; nothing was downloaded and the only tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The calculator recommends a package without showing its price, so you have to look up the price list yourself. The FNSKU label looked right on screen, but we did not print or scan it. The page says the images are PNG & EPS, not EPS and JPEG as in our dossier, and its comparison table gives GS1 US Direct a much lower starting price than our dossier; we did not check the GS1 US site, so treat both comparisons with care. Whether a reseller barcode works for your retailer is something the page itself asks you to check.

exit_test.what: No account was needed; the tool ran without signing in. On 18 November 2026 the session tested two free tools of Barcodes Talk without an account. The Barcode Quantity Calculator counted 6 codes for a product with 3 sizes and 2 colours in about a minute and recommended the package of 10 Barcodes, which costs $15.00 on the price list, though no price was shown next to the advice. The FNSKU label generator made an on-screen Amazon label for a made up code on an Avery 5160 sheet layout; it was not printed or scanned. The price list matches the dossier, but the page now says PNG & EPS images and gives a different GS1 US starting price than the dossier. Nothing was bought. Account and start: NO account was made and none was used; the free tools of Barcodes Talk run without signing in. Our AI assistant ran the test in our own tab of our browser, starting at 13:20. No cookie banner got in the way (there was a Your Privacy Choices link, not clicked). No e-mail address, phone number, password or card was typed in. The dossier name is Barcodes Talk and the review is on OSM (barcodes-talk-review). Core action 1, Barcode Quantity Calculator (barcodestalk.com/barcode-quantity-calculator), about 13:20 to 13:21, 1 minute, 4 steps: product Blue Snowboard, variation Size = 3 and Color = 2 (through + Add another variation type), Add Product. Result: Total Barcodes Needed 6 UPC/EAN codes, Breakdown Blue Snowboard 6, which is the right count (3 sizes times 2 colours). The tool recommended a package of 10 Barcodes, marked Best Match, with no price next to it, only a green Buy Barcodes button that was not clicked. On the price list 10 Barcodes cost $15.00. The page also shows the example T-Shirt (3 sizes, 4 colors), 12 barcodes needed. Core action 2, Amazon FNSKU label generator (barcodestalk.com/amazon-fnsku-barcode-label-generator), 13:21, 4 steps: the made up FNSKU code X00TEST001, product name Blue Snowboard, condition New, quantity 30 (the default) and the label format Avery 5160, 1" x 2.625" (30 labels/sheet), Amazon Recommended. Generate Label said Label generated successfully! and the preview showed a barcode with X00TEST001, Blue Snowboard and New. Nothing was saved or printed (Save Label, Save JPG and Print / PDF were not used), so the label was only seen on screen and was not scanned. Plans: The Buy Barcodes page (barcodestalk.com/buy-barcodes) was read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 and read again just before this delivery the same day, with the same prices: 1 Barcode $5.00, 5 Barcodes $10.00 ($2.00 ea), 10 Barcodes $15.00 ($1.50 ea), 25 Barcodes $25.00, 50 Barcodes $35.00, 100 Barcodes $45.00, 200 Barcodes $80.00, 500 Barcodes $125.00, 1,000 Barcodes $180.00, 1,500 $225.00, 2,000 $260.00, 2,500 $300.00, 5,000 $500.00, 10,000 $650.00, 25,000 $1,200.00, 50,000 $2,300.00, 75,000 $3,225.00 and 100,000 $3,500.00 ($0.035 ea). Included: UPC & EAN barcodes, PNG & EPS images, a Certificate of GTIN Assignment, Excel & PDF spreadsheets, Works for Amazon Guaranteed and No Renewal Fees or Hidden Charges. The prices match the dossier. No Buy Now button was clicked. Differences on the page against the dossier: the page lists PNG & EPS Images Included, while the dossier says EPS and JPEG. The comparison table on the page gives GS1 US Direct a starting price of US$30 for one GTIN and annual renewal fees of $0 for individual GTINs, with annual fees for Company Prefixes, while the dossier says $250 for 10 plus $50 a year. The site of GS1 US itself was not checked, so which figure is current is not known here. The page also says Accepted by 99% of retailers and asks you to check whether your retailer accepts reseller barcodes. Cancelling: there is no account and no subscription, so there was nothing to cancel. Not tested: a purchase and the checkout, the certificate, the GEPIR registration, the sample package (which may ask for an e-mail address), whether Amazon or Brand Registry accept the codes, a printed or scanned label, and the other free tools (bulk, SKU, QR, country of origin). Clean up: there is no account and no test data was saved; nothing was downloaded and the only tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The calculator recommends a package without showing its price, so you have to look up the price list yourself. The FNSKU label looked right on screen, but we did not print or scan it. The page says the images are PNG & EPS, not EPS and JPEG as in our dossier, and its comparison table gives GS1 US Direct a much lower starting price than our dossier; we did not check the GS1 US site, so treat both comparisons with care. Whether a reseller barcode works for your retailer is something the page itself asks you to check.
